headline: Colombian Peso Weakens as Dollar Tops 3,500 on Falling Crude
summary: The Colombian peso depreciated on Monday as the US dollar breached 3,500 pesos, driven by lower international oil prices and greenback strength that counteracted Wall Street gains.
why: Crude oil is Colombia's top export, making the peso exchange rate sensitive to Brent fluctuations.

impacts.name: Colombian peso
impacts.why: Weakened above 3,500 per dollar under pressure from falling oil prices.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: A drop of over 3% in crude oil prices and global dollar firmness weighed directly on the Colombian peso, pushing the dollar above 3,500 pesos.
